title: Far moves first, few moves last
hook: Can anything cut insertion sort's one-step shuffles?

knows: insertion sort slides each card left one step at a time (insertion-by-hand)
doesNotKnow: that sorting cards far apart first can save most of those steps

misconception: Insertion sort is slow because every step is needed; nothing can cut the number of one-step moves.
objective: The learner can explain that passes on far-apart cards carry cards most of the way in few moves, so on 16 reversed cards Shell sort with gaps 8, 4, 2, 1 makes 32 shifts against plain insertion sort's 120, because the final gap-1 pass finds every card one step from home.

claims.text: Plain insertion sort makes 120 shifts on 16 cards in exact reverse order.
claims.source: Builder's node script (2026-10-14, algo2-sc) and the PLAIN table in Demo.tsx: while (j >= 1 && a[j-1] > v) { a[j] = a[j-1]; j--; shifts++ } on 16 15 ... 1 gives 120 = 15 x 16 / 2. A shift is one card copied one place over. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own node gapped-insertion (g=1) on 16..1: 120 shifts = 15*16/2; matches PLAIN and the predict text.

claims.text: Shell sort with gaps 8, 4, 2, 1 on the same reversed hand makes 8 shifts in every pass, 32 in all.
claims.source: Builder's node script and the SHELL table in Demo.tsx: gapped insertion sort, while (j >= g && a[j-g] > v) { a[j] = a[j-g]; j -= g; shifts++ }, for g = 8, 4, 2, 1 on 16 15 ... 1: 8, 8, 8, 8 = 32. (Gaps 4, 1 give 48; not on the stage.) The stage replays each shift as a swap of the two cards g apart, which has the same count. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own node run, gaps 8,4,2,1: 8,8,8,8 = 32 shifts; the stage's swap-form loop also counts 32. Gaps 4,1 give 48.

claims.text: In the Shell lane the farthest card from its sorted place is 15 places away at the start, then 7 after the 8-apart pass, 3 after 4 apart, 1 after 2 apart and 0 after 1 apart.
claims.source: Builder's node script: max over positions i of |i - (value - 1)| after each pass: 15, 7, 3, 1, 0. Hands after each pass: 8 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 16 15 14 13 12 11 10 9; 4 3 2 1 8 7 6 5 12 11 10 9 16 15 14 13; 2 1 4 3 6 5 8 7 10 9 12 11 14 13 16 15; 1 ... 16. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own node: max |i-(v-1)| = 15, 7, 3, 1, 0 after each pass; hands match the builder's. Reveal prints 15, then 7, 3, 1; stage readout shows 0.

claims.text: When the gap reaches 1, every card is one step from home, so ordinary insertion sort has only 8 swaps left.
claims.source: Builder's node script: the hand before the gap-1 pass is 2 1 4 3 ... 16 15 (eight adjacent out-of-order pairs, farthest distance 1); the gap-1 pass makes 8 shifts. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Hand before gap 1 is 2 1 4 3 ... 16 15: every card exactly 1 from home; gap-1 pass makes 8 shifts (own run). Reveal says 'swaps' for shifts; same count.

claims.text: In plain insertion sort the 1 had to walk 15 places, one at a time.
claims.source: The 1 starts at position 16 of 16 and ends at position 1; each shift moves it (equivalently, moves one card past it) one place, so 15 shifts are spent on the 1's insertion alone. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own node: during plain insertion the 1's insertion makes 15 shifts (position 16 to 1).

claims.text: The last Shell pass (gap 1) is plain insertion sort, so the result is sorted whatever the earlier gaps were.
claims.source: Gapped insertion sort with g = 1 is exactly insertion sort, which sorts any input; earlier passes only permute the cards. Shell 1959, Commun. ACM 2(7); Knuth, TAOCP vol. 3, section 5.2.1 (from memory, not opened; check before publishing). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Derivation: the g=1 pass is insertion sort, which sorts any input. Shell 1959 (Commun. ACM 2(7), 30-32) and Knuth TAOCP vol. 3 sec. 5.2.1 placement correct to my knowledge; neither opened, and the sentence does not depend on them.

claims.text: A shift copies one card one gap to the right; gap 1 is ordinary insertion sort.
claims.source: Counting rule of this lesson (brief #41 and spec): one shift = one card copied one gap over, the inner-loop move of gapped insertion sort. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Matches the stage rule line and the inner loop of gapped insertion sort (definition).

recall.question: Shell sort runs insertion sort on cards far apart before the final ordinary insertion-sort pass. Why is that last pass cheap?
options: Every card is already near its place
The last pass only looks at half the cards
The far passes already sorted the list completely
recall.why: Far passes carry cards most of the way in big jumps, so ordinary insertion sort only has short, one-step moves left.
